_metadata.source: Curated country context for MAP workspace

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.summary: Largest OPEC producer (~10 mbpd) with ~3 mbpd of domestic refining, ~2.9 mbpd of effective Petroline bypass capacity, and systemically important Gulf export nodes at Ras Tanura and Ju'aymah.
countries.chokepointDependency: Partial Hormuz hedge via East-West (Petroline) pipeline to Yanbu; still core to Gulf-system export risk.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Saudi Arabia, plus Aramco annual report

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.summary: ADNOC-dominant exporter (~4 mbpd production) built around Murban as the primary light-sour grade. ADCOP (Habshan–Fujairah) delivers ~1.5 mbpd nameplate bypass capacity to the Gulf of Oman, insulating part of the export stream from Hormuz closure.
countries.chokepointDependency: Has bypass via Habshan–Fujairah (ADCOP) but remains tightly coupled to Gulf logistics and pricing context.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — UAE, October 2024; ADNOC fact sheet

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.summary: Major Gulf exporter (~2.7 mbpd production) centered on KNPC refining assets (Al Zour + legacy Mina Al-Ahmadi / Mina Abdulla / Shuaiba). Has no physical bypass and is entirely Hormuz-dependent for seaborne exports.
countries.chokepointDependency: Primarily Hormuz-dependent for seaborne exports; no bypass route exists.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Kuwait; KPC annual report

countries.name: Bahrain
countries.summary: Small producer (~0.2 mbpd) with Bapco's Sitra refinery as the dominant downstream asset. Directly pipeline-connected to Saudi Arabia's A-B pipeline from Khurais for feedstock, with all exports exiting the Gulf.
countries.chokepointDependency: Connected into the Gulf system and sensitive to regional export route disruptions; no bypass.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Bahrain; Bapco operator disclosures

countries.name: Iran
countries.summary: OPEC founding member producing ~3.4 mbpd under sustained US secondary sanctions. Crude exits via Kharg Island (~90% of flow) and Bandar Abbas — both inside the Strait of Hormuz. No physical bypass exists; the long-mooted Goreh–Jask line has never reached meaningful throughput.
countries.chokepointDependency: Entirely Hormuz-locked; no bypass route. Kharg Island and Bandar Abbas terminals both sit inside the strait.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Iran; NIOC disclosures (figures approximated given sanctions opacity)

countries.name: Iraq
countries.summary: Second-largest OPEC producer (~4.3 mbpd) with southern production dominating: Basra Oil Terminal + Khor al-Amaya carry ~3.3 mbpd of Hormuz-facing exports. The Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey's Mediterranean coast is a partial northern hedge at ~0.3 mbpd when political friction permits flow.
countries.chokepointDependency: Southern exports via Basra Oil Terminal are Hormuz-locked; the Kirkuk–Ceyhan line is a partial Mediterranean hedge for northern barrels but capacity is constrained by political friction.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Iraq, plus SOMO and trade-press estimates

countries.name: Qatar
countries.summary: Global LNG leader (~110 mtpa) with ~0.6 mbpd of crude and condensate production. All Qatari hydrocarbon exports transit the Strait of Hormuz via Ras Laffan (LNG), Halul Island (offshore crude), and Mesaieed (onshore crude + products). No bypass exists.
countries.chokepointDependency: All Qatari hydrocarbon exports transit Hormuz; no bypass exists. LNG and crude both exit via Ras Laffan and Halul Island terminals inside the strait.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Qatar; QatarEnergy annual report

countries.name: Oman
countries.summary: Non-OPEC producer (~1 mbpd) sitting physically east of the Strait of Hormuz. Mina al Fahal — the delivery point for the DME Oman futures contract and the global Asian-sour benchmark — is on the Gulf of Oman coast, so Omani crude never transits the chokepoint. In a Hormuz closure Oman becomes a natural hedge, not a casualty.
countries.chokepointDependency: Oman is east of the Strait of Hormuz. Mina al Fahal export terminal sits directly on the Gulf of Oman, giving Oman a natural hedge — Omani crude never transits the chokepoint.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Oman; PDO + OQ disclosures; DME contract specification

countries.name: Yemen
countries.summary: Civil conflict has collapsed Yemeni production from a ~0.44 mbpd peak in the mid-2000s to effectively near-zero today, with Little Aden refinery running below capacity. Historically exported Marib Light via Ras Isa (Red Sea) and Masila via Ash-Shihr (Gulf of Aden) — neither transits Hormuz but both carry Bab el-Mandeb exposure.
countries.chokepointDependency: Yemeni exports historically exit via Ras Isa (Red Sea → Bab el-Mandeb) and Ash-Shihr (Gulf of Aden, outside Hormuz). Zero Hormuz dependency but meaningful Bab el-Mandeb exposure.
countries.source: EIA Country Analysis Brief — Yemen; figures approximated given conflict-era reporting opacity
